title: Iterator protocol
description: An iterator is any object with a `.next()` method that returns `{ value, done }` — the contract `for...of` and spread rely on.

notes: `.next()` MUST return an object shaped `{ value, done }` — booleans for done, anything for value.
Once `done: true` is returned, calling `.next()` again should keep returning done — iterators are one-shot.
`Symbol.iterator` (not a string) is the well-known key for iterable lookup — `obj[Symbol.iterator]`.

questions.q: What shape must an iterator's `.next()` return?
options: { value, done, index } — index is required so spread can preserve sparse holes
Just the value, with iteration terminated by returning `undefined`
[value, done] — a tuple, matching destructuring conventions
questions.explain: The iterator protocol requires an object with `value` and `done` properties.

questions.q: Which is true about iterators vs iterables?
options: An iterable has [Symbol.iterator]() that returns an iterator
An iterator wraps an iterable via [Symbol.iterable]
